title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 7

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the process planning class take place?
tasks.audioText: The manufacturing planning class will review a sample process sheet on Monday at ten. Students should bring the component drawing and the operation list. The instructor will explain how a process sheet connects the required geometry with the sequence of manufacturing stages. Detailed machine settings will not be discussed in this classroom exercise.
options: On Monday at ten
On Monday at nine
On Tuesday at ten
On Monday at eleven

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which documents are needed for the process-planning class?
tasks.audioText: The manufacturing planning class will review a sample process sheet on Monday at ten. Students should bring the component drawing and the operation list. The instructor will explain how a process sheet connects the required geometry with the sequence of manufacturing stages. Detailed machine settings will not be discussed in this classroom exercise.
options: The process chart and risk assessment
The component drawing and operation list
The maintenance manual and calibration record
The material certificate and parts catalogue

tasks.prompt: A process plan describes the main stages required to produce a component. It may identify the operation, the equipment category and the inspection point. The sequence should reflect the component's design and the requirements in the approved documentation. A clear plan also helps the production team understand which stage has been completed and what needs to happen next. Reading 1. What may a process plan identify?
options: The supplier, batch number and purchase price
The operator, shift pattern and delivery date
The operation, equipment category and inspection point
The material colour, storage area and order quantity
It reduces the cost of every operation
It removes the need to check the component drawing
It identifies the supplier's preferred equipment
It reflects the design and helps the team follow the stages

tasks.prompt: The inspection point ___ in the process plan.
options: is identified
identify
identifying
are identify

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO technical entries that define the sequence and verification stages in a machining process plan.
options: Supplier payment terms
Operator's annual leave balance
Operation description
Inspection point

tasks.prompt: A planned series of manufacturing stages is a process ___.
A process stage is missing from the plan. What should you ask?
options: I will add a stage without checking.
Could we review the sequence against the component drawing?
The sequence does not matter.
I will remove the inspection stage.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of process planning in a logical order.
options: Arrange the stages in a logical sequence
Review the component drawing
Add relevant inspection points
Identify the required operations
correctOrder: Arrange the stages in a logical sequence

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how a process plan helps a manufacturing team organise work and communicate progress.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response explains the purpose of a process plan for organising manufacturing work (0–2); it describes how sequence, resources or inspection points help the team communicate progress (0–2); the explanation is clearly structured with understandable grammar (0–2); process-planning/production vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
